about: Dub's logger (@axiomhq/logging 0.1.5 over @axiomhq/js 1.3.1) as the World bench runs it, with the World's Axiom token and dataset: its batches land through the legacy ingest and each event is kept as the vendor's record; the account's datasets are read back by the dataset list; every other operation is the gap.

decisions.demand: Dub's logger flushes each batch (apps/web/lib/axiom/server.ts:31, AxiomJSTransport; @axiomhq/js@1.3.1:dist/esm/client.js:43 POST /v1/datasets/<dataset>/ingest, application/x-ndjson); the World bench's evidence reads the stored events (twin-world ADR 0036, What changes).
decisions.why: Reads the body by its Content-Type (JSON, NDJSON, CSV), applies event labels, the timestamp field and format, reserved-name renames and field limits, refuses an unknown dataset (404), a token without access to it (403) and an all-rejected request (400), and keeps each accepted event as an `event` (_time, _sysTime, _rowId, data) under its dataset. Answers IngestStatus: ingested, failed, failures, processedBytes, blocksCreated, walLength; the SDK reads none of them but a 4xx's message (fetchClient.js:38). journeys/first-use.json asserts the status's ingested count and the dataset in the list.

The spec names DatasetSpec as its answer and the derived core lists the account's datasets as stored (id, name, description, who, created); journeys/first-use.json's readback lists the dataset the World issued.

decisions.demand: World account credentials for app logging (AXIOM_TOKEN, AXIOM_DATASET).
decisions.why: Account bootstrap: the dataset the application ingests into and a basic API token with ingest access to it, as Axiom's console makes them (Datasets > New dataset; Settings > API tokens), the same at every boot.
